I hope I still feel this way tomorrow: C.name: I hope I still feel this way tomorrow: Charlene Liu
I hope I still feel this way tomorrow: C.description: Elizabeth Leach Gallery is excited to present I hope I still feel this way tomorrow, an exhibition of new work made by Eugene-based artist Charlene Liu. Liu’s fifth solo show with the gallery traverses painted and printed mediums and utilizes a variety of techniques to materialize the intangible,...

UnEarthed: Nicola L\u00f3pez-Elizabeth L.name: UnEarthed: Nicola López
UnEarthed: Nicola L\u00f3pez-Elizabeth L.description: Santa Fe-based artist Nicola López channels her transdisciplinary interests in urban planning, architecture, and anthropology into a multimedia practice spanning drawing, printmaking, installation, and hand-drawn animated video. López interjects and interacts with the photographed natural environment, layering upon these images a geometric, structural landscape of her imagination. The hollow contours...

Sean Cain: Mysterious Barricades-Russo L.name: Sean Cain: Mysterious Barricades
Sean Cain: Mysterious Barricades-Russo L.description: Russo Lee Gallery is pleased to present Mysterious Barricades, an exhibition by Sean Cain. This body of paintings marks his first solo show in several years. Exploring what he calls “eventful stillness, still eventfulness,” Cain brings together still life and narrative figure painting, allowing each genre to take on the qualities of the other.

Lucinda Parker: D\u00e9j\u00e0 Vu All Ov.name: Lucinda Parker: Déjà Vu All Over Again
Lucinda Parker: D\u00e9j\u00e0 Vu All Ov.description: For the month of November, Russo Lee Gallery presents Déjà Vu All Over Again by Lucinda Parker. Spanning more than six decades, this exhibition celebrates a major retrospective from 1965 to 2026, bringing together a remarkable period of sustained creativity, and an artist whose work has been shaped by observation, experimentation, mentorship, and an enduring curiosity about the world.

Ren\u00e9 Rickabaugh: Reflections-Russo.name: René Rickabaugh: Reflections
Ren\u00e9 Rickabaugh: Reflections-Russo.description: Russo Lee Gallery is pleased to present Reflections by René Rickabaugh. This exhibition celebrates over five decades of the artist's compelling body of work, bringing together a collection that showcases his exceptional artistic vision and creative practice.

Northwest Masters: Works from Estates &.name: Northwest Masters: Works from Estates & Private Collections
Northwest Masters: Works from Estates &.description: For the month of December, Russo Lee Gallery presents Northwest Masters: Works from Estates & Private Collections. This group exhibition features a selection of works by influential Pacific Northwest artists who have helped shape Portland’s art scene and establish the foundation of the region’s artistic legacy.

Laurie Danial: Beauty and the Long Walk.name: Laurie Danial: Beauty and the Long Walk Home
Laurie Danial: Beauty and the Long Walk.description: Froelick Gallery is pleased to present Laurie Danial’s latest body of work, Beauty and The Long Walk Home. A solo exhibit of recent paintings on panel and paper. Laurie Danial's abstractions are process-driven; her work is intuitive, experimental, and dictated by her day-to-day concerns, visual experiences, and collected ephemera...

Daniel Robinson: Promised Land-Froelick.name: Daniel Robinson: Promised Land
Daniel Robinson: Promised Land-Froelick.description: Froelick Gallery is honored to present Daniel Robinson’s most recent paintings, marking the profound continuation of his decades-long engagement with agrarian landscapes and industrial architecture in the American West. Born in 1963 in Buffalo, New York, Robinson has spent over thirty years creating enduring images of our built, natural and...

Confidants: Rick Bartow and Seiichi Hiro.name: Confidants: Rick Bartow and Seiichi Hiroshima

Sally Cleveland \u2013 a Small Yellow Tr.name: Sally Cleveland – a Small Yellow Tree / Recent Paintings

Photorealism: Joe Rudko-PDX Contemporary.name: Photorealism: Joe Rudko
Photorealism: Joe Rudko-PDX Contemporary.description: A few years ago, I might have wondered when or where a photograph was taken. Now, I ask: is it real? If photographs are no longer understood as reliable records of reality, then the definition of photorealism changes. If photographs are fragmented, altered, and generated, then what does it mean to make a photorealistic painting?

Ashley Pe\u00f1a-Blue Sky Gallery.name: Ashley Peña
Ashley Pe\u00f1a-Blue Sky Gallery.description: Ebb and Flow moves between worlds, histories, and states of being. Set in Ayiti-Kiskeya (Haiti and Dominican Republic), the exhibition explores the entanglements of memory and erasure, belonging, grief and renewal; considering how colonial histories haunt the present, marcating the landscapes through which we move and the lives we carry. These histories– neither distant nor finished– persist and are carried forth by living and the ancestral presences that continue to inhabit our world.

Yukai Chen-Blue Sky Gallery.name: Yukai Chen
Yukai Chen-Blue Sky Gallery.description: The Factory of Desire explores queer identity, belonging, and cultural inheritance through self-portraits and staged photographs. Drawing on the artist’s upbringing in a rural village within a religious yet rapidly modernizing city in southeastern China, the series transforms personal experiences of displacement into constructed queer spaces.

How We Show Up: Oregon Jews in Civil Soc.name: How We Show Up: Oregon Jews in Civil Society, An America 250 Exhibition
How We Show Up: Oregon Jews in Civil Soc.venue: Oregon Jewish Museum and Center for Holocaust Education
How We Show Up: Oregon Jews in Civil Soc.description: What does civic participation look like? How do communities shape the places where they live? How We Show Up explores the many ways Jews in Oregon have participated in public life—from building towns and holding office in the nineteenth century to advocating for civil rights, immigrant communities, and social justice...

One Nation-Oregon Jewish Museum and Cent.name: One Nation
One Nation-Oregon Jewish Museum and Cent.venue: Oregon Jewish Museum and Center for Holocaust Education
One Nation-Oregon Jewish Museum and Cent.description: One Nation brings together contemporary artists who explore the ideals and contradictions embedded in the American promise. Drawing on the national motto E Pluribus Unum — “Out of Many, One” — the exhibition reflects on how a diverse society strives toward unity while confronting social, political, and cultural divisions....

Frank Stella: Had Gadya-Oregon Jewish Mu.name: Frank Stella: Had Gadya
Frank Stella: Had Gadya-Oregon Jewish Mu.venue: Oregon Jewish Museum and Center for Holocaust Education
Frank Stella: Had Gadya-Oregon Jewish Mu.description: In 1981, American artist Frank Stella encountered El Lissitzky’s 1919 illustrations of Had Gadya at the Tel Aviv Museum and found an unexpected source of inspiration. Drawn to the Russian-Jewish artist’s use of abstraction to tell the familiar Passover story, Stella spent the next several years developing his own response. The resulting 12 prints, created...

The Stars We Do Not See: Australian Indi.name: The Stars We Do Not See: Australian Indigenous Art
The Stars We Do Not See: Australian Indi.description: This eye-opening exhibition introduces North American audiences to the diverse and distinct visual iconographies of Indigenous Australia, which is made up of more than 250 distinct Indigenous nations.

Mickalene Thomas: Do I Look Like a Lady?.name: Mickalene Thomas: Do I Look Like a Lady? (Comedians and Singers)
Mickalene Thomas: Do I Look Like a Lady?.description: The Portland Art Museum is pleased to present the recently acquired two-channel video installation, Do I Look Like a Lady? (Comedians and Singers), by internationally renowned artist Mickalene Thomas. Thomas’s work addresses themes of beauty and identity expressed through the myriad subjectivities of African-American women. Her multidisciplinary practice reconsiders Black womanhood and desire through a queer lens.

Abstraction Since Mark Rothko-Portland A.name: Abstraction Since Mark Rothko
Abstraction Since Mark Rothko-Portland A.description: A companion to The Art of Mark Rothko, this exhibition presents the vitality of abstract painting in American art from Rothko’s time to the present.

Facing Ourselves-Portland Art Museum.name: Facing Ourselves
Facing Ourselves-Portland Art Museum.description: Portraiture is about truth and honesty, both in how we choose to have ourselves portrayed and in how artists present their subjects. During the Renaissance, portraiture was tied to humanism, which values the individual.

For the Enjoyment of All: Celebrating th.name: For the Enjoyment of All: Celebrating the Kress Gift
For the Enjoyment of All: Celebrating th.description: In 1952, the Portland Art Museum was given a spectacular selection of European art by the Samuel H. Kress Foundation in New York.

Black Arts PDX at the CREATE SPACE-Portl.name: Black Arts PDX at the CREATE SPACE
Black Arts PDX at the CREATE SPACE-Portl.description: A display of ephemera and an extended documentary trailer foregrounding the history of the Black visual arts community in Northeast Portland.

Heaven and Earth: Chinese Art from the C.name: Heaven and Earth: Chinese Art from the Collections
Heaven and Earth: Chinese Art from the C.description: Heaven and Earth spotlights powerful works of art in the Museum’s collections, spanning creative practices in China across several millennia.

American Land-Portland Art Museum.name: American Land
American Land-Portland Art Museum.description: Landscape painting has always had a unique place in the history of American Art. Earlier settlers and colonists especially celebrated the American landscape – one that has been shaped by the stewardship of Native peoples through the ages.

Mirror Mirror: Silver in the 20th Centur.name: Mirror Mirror: Silver in the 20th Century
Mirror Mirror: Silver in the 20th Centur.description: Silver has had special status in European and world art for thousands of years. Besides coins and jewelry, silver was used for objects of practical use, and families often held their wealth in a collection of silver spoons, teapots and other items.

Myth and Memory: Mediterranean Antiquity.name: Myth and Memory: Mediterranean Antiquity and its Revivals
Myth and Memory: Mediterranean Antiquity.description: The ancient Greeks loved wall murals and small portable paintings, but most of these have been lost over time. Instead, their art is best known from objects such as ceramic pots and vessels, excavated from rubbish heaps and graves. These ordinary household wares were produced in vast quantity, and some were even decorated by artists of extraordinary talent.

Mystic Mountain: Mount Hood in Art-Portl.name: Mystic Mountain: Mount Hood in Art
Mystic Mountain: Mount Hood in Art-Portl.description: Mount Hood’s iconic form, isolated presence on the horizon, and impressive height all serve to mark the natural monument as home for Portlanders.

Harriet Tubman Center Museum-Portland Ar.name: Harriet Tubman Center Museum
Harriet Tubman Center Museum-Portland Ar.description: Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary

Lisa Jarrett: Tenderhead-Portland Art Mu.name: Lisa Jarrett: Tenderhead
Lisa Jarrett: Tenderhead-Portland Art Mu.description: Lisa Jarrett weaves together her interest in migration and tracing lost familial histories to Beauty Supply stores and salons—critical intersections of Black life.

Forming Nature, Nature Formed-Portland A.name: Forming Nature, Nature Formed
Forming Nature, Nature Formed-Portland A.description: The inaugural exhibition in the heart of the Rothko Pavilion speaks to the strong sense of place experienced through our connection to our natural environment. Drawn from the Asian, Native American, Northwest, and Modern and Contemporary Art collections, Forming Nature, Nature Formed features artworks in glass, clay, metal, neon, and wood that speak to the ways artists from many cultural backgrounds interpret encounters with the natural world in sculptural form.

Todd McGrain: Debut of York-Portland Art.name: Todd McGrain: Debut of York
Todd McGrain: Debut of York-Portland Art.description: Todd McGrain’s original bust of York, the enslaved man who was the only African American member of the Lewis and Clark expedition, was secretly installed on Mount Tabor in 2021. It was placed on the pedestal where a statue of Oregonian editor Harvey Scott (1830-1910), a known racist, once stood.

Pipilotti Rist: 4th Floor to Mildness-Po.name: Pipilotti Rist: 4th Floor to Mildness
Pipilotti Rist: 4th Floor to Mildness-Po.description: Pipilotti Rist dissolves exhibition spaces through luminous color, moving imagery, and melodic sound. 4th Floor to Mildness immerses us in a soft, aquatically inspired environment, where a film shot underwater plays across two biomorphic-shaped screens hanging from the ceiling.

Marco Brambilla: Maximalist Dreamscapes-.name: Marco Brambilla: Maximalist Dreamscapes
Marco Brambilla: Maximalist Dreamscapes-.description: High-definition 3D 8K video with sound, color; 5 min., 45 sec., loop A lavish and satirical take on the silver-screen spectacle of Hollywood dreams and excesses, Heaven’s Gate both celebrates collective storytelling and satirizes saturated glamour and stereotypes. The continuously looping video ascends through the seven levels of purgatory, each stage its own unique landscape of visual samples lifted from iconic moments in cinematic history.

Nine Women Artists-Portland Art Museum.name: Nine Women Artists
Nine Women Artists-Portland Art Museum.description: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting.

An Honest Day\u2019s Work: Photographs o.name: An Honest Day’s Work: Photographs of Labor
An Honest Day\u2019s Work: Photographs o.description: Drawn from the permanent collection, this exhibition explores an expansive concept of work, from manual labor to art creation and childcare–forms of work that often go unrecognized in contemporary society.

A Brief History of Photography: The Port.name: A Brief History of Photography: The Portrait
A Brief History of Photography: The Port.description: This mini-history of photography demonstrates the importance of the photographic portrait, beginning with the medium’s commercial inception in the mid-19th century and through to the present day.

Imagine Monuments: A Partnership with Ar.name: Imagine Monuments: A Partnership with Arts in Education of the Gorge
Imagine Monuments: A Partnership with Ar.description: What is the purpose of a public monument? To whom does it belong? How does a monument remind us of what we care about and who we are as a community? If you designed a monument, what would it look or feel or sound like? What story would it tell?

To Gather Your Leaving: Themes of Diaspo.name: To Gather Your Leaving: Themes of Diasporic Experiences in the Northwest
To Gather Your Leaving: Themes of Diaspo.description: Covering a span of a hundred years, the Portland Art Museum’s Northwest collection represents a rich tapestry of work created from the experiences of movement, migration, displacement, hope, home, memory, and loss.

Here we are-Portland Art Museum.name: Here we are
Here we are-Portland Art Museum.description: Here we are surveys contemporary art from the Portland Art Museum’s collection. Featuring work across a range of media, the exhibition showcases recent acquisitions alongside signature works and reflects on the constant change and shifting narratives that mark our contemporary world and networked lives.

MAKERS: The Culture of Craft-Portland Ar.name: MAKERS: The Culture of Craft
MAKERS: The Culture of Craft-Portland Ar.description: Galleries 106, 107 Makers illuminates the virtuosity of maker and material in Japan. Looking across time periods, this exhibition explores the porous boundaries between art, craft, design, and labor. Works on […]

The Art of Mark Rothko-Portland Art Muse.name: The Art of Mark Rothko
The Art of Mark Rothko-Portland Art Muse.description: This exhibition features a concise, chronological display of works by the renowned American artist Mark Rothko. The Museum’s new entrance pavilion is named in honor of the artist.

Conversations in Clay-Portland Art Museu.name: Conversations in Clay
Conversations in Clay-Portland Art Museu.description: Gallery 109 Conversations in Clay presents a glimpse of the diverse range of directions in contemporary ceramics in Japan. Emphasizing natural ash glazes, sculptural forms, and meticulous surface treatments, it explores […]

Highest Heaven-Portland Art Museum.name: Highest Heaven
Highest Heaven-Portland Art Museum.description: Elvin A. Duerst’s gift of works from the Spanish viceregal or colonial period in Central and South America from 1521 until the revolutions led by Simon Bolivar liberated these areas from Spanish control in 1821.

Black Art and Experiences-Portland Art M.name: Black Art and Experiences
Black Art and Experiences-Portland Art M.description: The Black Art and Experiences (B.A.E.) Galleries are a gallery floor dedicated to celebrating the breadth, depth, and vitality of Black artistic expression.

Word in Flower: Arts of Buddhism-Portlan.name: Word in Flower: Arts of Buddhism
Word in Flower: Arts of Buddhism-Portlan.description: Featuring sculpture, calligraphy, painting, photography, and more, the exhibition explores diverse expressions of Buddhist visual culture in this region from the 6th to 21st centuries.

Watanabe Sadao-Portland Art Museum.name: Watanabe Sadao
Watanabe Sadao-Portland Art Museum.description: This exhibition introduces the artistry of Watanabe Sadao (1913–1996), who developed a unique stencil printing process based on traditional Japanese textile dyeing techniques.

Mary Henry: A Long Unbroken Line-Portlan.name: Mary Henry: A Long Unbroken Line
Mary Henry: A Long Unbroken Line-Portlan.description: Mary Henry embraced geometry as relational to the structures and environments around us.

Rick Bartow: Storyteller-Portland Art Mu.name: Rick Bartow: Storyteller
Rick Bartow: Storyteller-Portland Art Mu.description: Bartow’s gift as a visual storyteller takes us on a narrative journey: his self-portraits tell stories of pain, memory, and self-discovery; others reflect on his Wiyot identity, Native history and culture; and his portrayals of beings who walk on four legs, swim, or fly deftly capture their essence.

Shifting the Narrative: 21st Century Acq.name: Shifting the Narrative: 21st Century Acquisitions
Shifting the Narrative: 21st Century Acq.description: Shifting the Narrative: 21st Century Acquisitions highlights Native American art gifts and purchases since the year 2000 at the Portland Art Museum.

Global Impressionism-Portland Art Museum.name: Global Impressionism
Global Impressionism-Portland Art Museum.description: In 1874, a group of French artists organized the first exhibition of sketch-like avant-garde paintings at a private gallery in Paris. Critics gave them the unflattering label “Impressionist” because of their sketchlike works, but the artists embraced the terms and exhibited under this name for another seven shows. Their use of broken strokes of often pure color, is often seen as typically French but in fact became a global phenomenon.

Im/Material-Portland Art Museum.name: Im/Material
Im/Material-Portland Art Museum.description: From the 1960s onward, artists engaged in a vibrant expansion of stylistic approaches, idea-driven practices, and material exploration. In some circles, they embraced the value of concepts as the foundation for their art, placing significance on the intellectual over the final appearance of the artwork.

Yinka Ilori: Mountains Full of Blessings.name: Yinka Ilori: Mountains Full of Blessings
Yinka Ilori: Mountains Full of Blessings.description: Internationally acclaimed British-Nigerian artist Yinka Ilori, MBE, known for his colorful, "joy-led" design philosophy, has designed a monumental work of asphalt art to fill the street.

Prints of Darkness: The Modern Mezzotint.name: Prints of Darkness: The Modern Mezzotint
Prints of Darkness: The Modern Mezzotint.description: Prized for its ability to create velvety, dark, and subtle surfaces, mezzotint is a printmaking process in which the artist works from dark to light, coaxing the image from the shadows.

Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness.name: Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print
Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness.description: Inspired by W.E.B. Du Bois’s legacy, this exhibition brings together leading Black contemporary artists who use printmaking, sculpture, installation, textile, and video to interrogate the intersections of race, technology, and representation in a data-driven society.

German Expressionism in Art and Film-Por.name: German Expressionism in Art and Film
German Expressionism in Art and Film-Por.description: German Expressionism in Art and Film immerses visitors in the dramatic world of German art and film that developed during the turbulent years between the end of World War I and the Nazi Party’s political and cultural domination of Germany in the 1930s.

Titus Kaphar: Ascension-Portland Art Mus.name: Titus Kaphar: Ascension
Titus Kaphar: Ascension-Portland Art Mus.description: Ascension marks Kaphar’s most expansive exploration of spirituality to date. Where much of his work has examined the histories we inherit and who has been erased from them, Ascension turns toward what carries us beyond them.

M. C. Escher: Infinite Variations-Portla.name: M. C. Escher: Infinite Variations
M. C. Escher: Infinite Variations-Portla.description: The exhibition includes early figure drawings, lesser-known book illustrations, detailed Italian landscapes, transformations in which fish morph into birds, and the birds morph into horses, and his signature architectural fantasies in which stairways seem to go both up and down.

Gons: The Pictures, Mechanisms, and Came.name: Gons: The Pictures, Mechanisms, and Camera Works of Doug Wing
Gons: The Pictures, Mechanisms, and Came.description: Gons: The Pictures, Mechanisms and Camera Works of Doug Wing, curated by Kristan Kennedy, is a retrospective exhibition celebrating Wing's decades-long creative career. Running from November 4 through December 19, 2026, at Oregon Contemporary, the show highlights his multi-medium artistic journey and includes a mini-documentary directed by filmmaker Jonathan Marrs.

Thought Forms: Open Studio-Oregon Contem.name: Thought Forms: Open Studio
Thought Forms: Open Studio-Oregon Contem.description: Thought Forms draws inspiration from two seemingly disparate sources: an esoteric book by Annie Besant and C. W. Leadbeater, titled Thought-Forms (1901), that illustrates thoughts and emotions as materialized shapes and colors, and the banners hung outside Southside Presbyterian Church in Tucson, AZ, in 1982, declaring sanctuary for Central American refugees. Together, these sources inspire a process in which collective declarations can take form, shape, and action.

Rose Salane: Afterlife in Public-Cooley.name: Rose Salane: Afterlife in Public
Rose Salane: Afterlife in Public-Cooley.description: The Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery, Reed College, and Converge 45 present Afterlife in Public, a newly commissioned exhibition featuring a multi-channel video installation developed in Portland by artist Rose Salane.
